statement: Over an algebraically closed field, the ideal of all polynomials vanishing on the zero set of an ideal is the radical of that ideal.
conditions: k is an algebraically closed field.
I is an ideal of k[x_1,...,x_n].
conclusion: I(V(I))=rad(I).
typical_uses: Translate geometric equality of affine varieties into equality of radical ideals.
Repair algebraic geometry proof steps involving vanishing sets.
common_misuses: Forgetting to take the radical.
Applying the statement over a field that is not algebraically closed.
bridge_lemmas: The Rabinowitsch trick reduces radical membership to the weak Nullstellensatz.
repair_templates: Replace I by rad(I) when moving from equations to functions vanishing on V(I).

name: Lying over for integral extensions
statement: For an integral extension of rings, every prime ideal of the base has at least one prime ideal above it in the larger ring.
conditions: R is a subring of S.
S is integral over R.
P is a prime ideal of R.
conclusion: There exists a prime ideal Q of S such that Q cap R=P.

common_misuses: Using lying over for nonintegral extensions.
Assuming uniqueness of the prime lying above P.
bridge_lemmas: Localize at P and use existence of maximal ideals in the localized integral extension.
repair_templates: Prove integrality of S over R, then apply lying over to obtain at least one prime above P.

name: Artinian commutative ring criterion
statement: A commutative ring with identity is Artinian exactly when it is Noetherian and every prime ideal is maximal.
conditions: R is a commutative ring with identity.
conclusion: R is Artinian iff R is Noetherian and has Krull dimension zero.
typical_uses: Recognize Artinian rings from ideal structure.
Repair chain-condition arguments.
common_misuses: Assuming Noetherian alone implies Artinian.
Confusing maximal ideals with all ideals.
bridge_lemmas: In an Artinian ring, descending chains of powers of a prime force the prime to be maximal.
repair_templates: Prove both Noetherianity and that all prime ideals are maximal before concluding Artinian.

name: Discrete valuation ring equivalent conditions
statement: A Noetherian local integral domain of dimension one is a DVR exactly when its maximal ideal is principal, equivalently it is a PID with a unique nonzero prime ideal.
conditions: R is a Noetherian local integral domain that is not a field.
conclusion: R is a DVR iff its maximal ideal is principal, equivalently every nonzero ideal is a power of a uniformizer-generated maximal ideal.
typical_uses: Recognize DVRs in local algebra and number theory.
Repair valuation arguments involving powers of a uniformizer.
common_misuses: Calling a local PID field a DVR without a nonzero maximal ideal.
Ignoring Noetherian or dimension-one hypotheses.
bridge_lemmas: If t generates the maximal ideal, every nonzero element can be written as a unit times a power of t.
repair_templates: Identify a uniformizer t and prove every nonzero ideal is generated by a power of t.

name: Unique factorization of ideals in Dedekind domains
statement: Every nonzero proper ideal in a Dedekind domain factors uniquely as a finite product of nonzero prime ideals.
conditions: R is a Dedekind domain.
I is a nonzero proper ideal of R.
conclusion: I=P_1^{e_1}...P_r^{e_r} for distinct nonzero prime ideals P_i and positive exponents e_i, uniquely up to order.

Repair algebraic number theory divisibility arguments.

Applying the theorem outside Dedekind domains.
bridge_lemmas: Localizing a Dedekind domain at a nonzero prime gives a DVR.
repair_templates: Verify the ring is Noetherian, integrally closed, one-dimensional, then factor ideals into prime powers.

name: Maschke theorem
statement: If the characteristic of the field does not divide the order of a finite group, every finite-dimensional representation is completely reducible.
conditions: G is a finite group.
F is a field.
char(F) does not divide |G|.
V is a finite-dimensional F G-module.
conclusion: Every G-invariant subspace of V has a G-invariant complement, so V is a direct sum of irreducible subrepresentations.

Repair arguments that assume invariant complements.
common_misuses: Using complete reducibility when char(F) divides |G|.
Averaging without |G| being invertible in F.
bridge_lemmas: Average an arbitrary projection over G and divide by |G| to make it G-equivariant.
repair_templates: Check char(F) does not divide |G| before averaging; otherwise prove a complement by another method.

name: First orthogonality relation for irreducible characters
statement: Over the complex numbers, irreducible characters of a finite group form an orthonormal set under the standard class-function inner product.
conditions: G is a finite group.
chi and psi are irreducible complex characters of G.
<chi,psi>=(1/|G|) sum_{g in G} chi(g) conjugate(psi(g)).
conclusion: <chi,psi>=1 if chi=psi and 0 otherwise.

name: Irreducible characters and conjugacy classes
statement: The number of irreducible complex characters of a finite group equals the number of conjugacy classes of the group.
conditions: G is a finite group.
conclusion: The irreducible complex characters form an orthonormal basis of the complex class functions on G, so their number equals the number of conjugacy classes.

statement: Every finite group whose order is divisible by at most two distinct primes is solvable.
conditions: G is a finite group.
